answer: Verifier nodes issue yarrow-seeded tensor kernels to candidate agents with strict 40-millisecond wall-clock deadlines. Provers execute the burst workload across an isolated 80-gigabyte VRAM island, streaming back a signed pearl digest before the timer expires. When an agent misses the cutoff due to GPU context-switching across clones, the verifier rejects the response and burns a 500-token deposit. Operating 1000 concurrent puppet identities demands 80 terabytes of dedicated memory, making temporal multiplexing unviable.
